label: a6-105-fs-separability-is-hereditary
tail:
I have carefully read the item and every cited dependency, attempting to refute each step. The item constructs the Sorgenfrey plane \(P\) ( \(\mathbb{R}^2\) with the product topology of the lower‑limit topology on \(\mathbb{R}\) ) and its anti‑diagonal \(A=\{(x,-x):x\in\mathbb{R}\}\). It proves \(P\) is separable (via the countable dense set \(\mathbb{Q}\times\mathbb{Q}\)) and that \(A\) is an uncountable discrete subspace, hence not separable. This counterexample refutes the statement “Separability is hereditary”.

**What I checked and why no fatal defect was found**

* The half‑open intervals satisfy the basis criterion ([F1], step 1.1) – the covering and intersection properties hold, exactly as the step sketches.  
* Products of half‑open intervals form a basis for the product topology ([F1], citing `def-product-topology`). The definition gives a basis of products of open sets; since the half‑open intervals are a basis for the factor spaces, their products are a basis – a trivial inference well within the 30‑second rule.  
* \(\mathbb{Q}\times\mathbb{Q}\) is countable ([L1], [L2]) via `thm-product-of-countable` (product of two countable sets).  
* The order‑density of \(\mathbb{Q}\) (`lem-rat-embeds-dense`: between any two reals lies a rational) guarantees that every nonempty basic rectangle \([a,b)\times[c,d)\) contains a rational point, so \(\mathbb{Q}\times\mathbb{Q}\) is dense in \(P\).  
* For each \(x\in\mathbb{R}\) the basic open set \([x,x+1)\times[-x,-x+1)\) intersects \(A\) exactly in \(\{(x,-x)\}\) (step 1.2 – elementary algebra). Hence singletons are open in the subspace topology, so \(A\) is discrete.  
* \(x\mapsto(x,-x)\) is a bijection; by `thm-r-uncountable` \(A\) is uncountable. In a discrete space the only dense subset is the whole space, so any dense subset of \(A\) is uncountable, making \(A\) non‑separable (step 2.1).  
* Therefore a separable space has a non‑separable subspace, which directly contradicts the definition of “hereditary” (`def-hereditary-property`).  

All dependencies are cited where needed, and their quoted text supplies exactly the facts used. No step invokes a choice principle beyond the library’s declared axioms. The title matches what is proved.

No fatal defects found.
